title: Von Neumann closure, standard vectors and modular analytic tools

items.title: Concrete von Neumann algebra and faithful vector
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and
$\mathcal B(H)$ the space of bounded linear operators on $H$
([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]). For a set
$\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$, write

$$\mathcal S':=\{T\in\mathcal B(H):Ts=sT\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S\}, \qquad \mathcal S'':=(\mathcal S')'.$$

The strong operator topology on $\mathcal B(H)$ is the topology of pointwise
norm convergence: $T_\alpha\to T$ strongly exactly when
$\|(T_\alpha-T)\xi\|\to0$ for every $\xi\in H$. The weak operator topology is
the topology of pointwise matrix-coefficient convergence: $T_\alpha\to T$
weakly exactly when $\langle T_\alpha\xi,\eta\rangle\to\langle T\xi,\eta\rangle$
for every $\xi,\eta\in H$. Use the linear-first inner-product convention.

A **concrete von Neumann algebra** on $H$ is a unital star subalgebra
$M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ satisfying $M=M''$. Under Choice, the double
commutant theorem makes this equivalent to being closed in the weak operator
topology.

An operator $a\in\mathcal B(H)$ is **positive** when $a=a^*$ and
$\langle a\xi,\xi\rangle\ge0$ for every $\xi\in H$, using the bounded
adjoint convention of [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]]. Write $M_+$ for the
positive operators in $M$ and $a\le b$ when $b-a$ is positive.

A vector $\Omega\in H$ is **cyclic** for $M$ when
$\overline{M\Omega}=H$, and is **separating** for $M$ when
$x\Omega=0$ for $x\in M$ implies $x=0$. For a unit vector $\Omega$, define its
vector functional by $\omega_\Omega(x)=\langle x\Omega,\Omega\rangle$.
It is **faithful** when $\omega_\Omega(x^*x)=0$ implies $x=0$; this is
equivalent to $\Omega$ being separating because
$\omega_\Omega(x^*x)=\|x\Omega\|^2$.

For a bounded linear functional $\varphi:M\to\mathbb C$, **positive** means
$\varphi(a)\ge0$ for every $a\in M_+$. A positive functional is **normal**
when $\varphi(\sup_\alpha x_\alpha)=\sup_\alpha\varphi(x_\alpha)$ for each
bounded increasing net $(x_\alpha)$ in $M_+$ whose supremum is taken in $M$.

items.title: Conjugate Hilbert space and adjoint of an antilinear operator
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. All inner products are linear in their first
argument. If $H$ is a complex Hilbert space, its **conjugate Hilbert space**
$\overline H$ consists of symbols $\overline x$ for $x\in H$, with
$\overline x+\overline y=\overline{x+y}$,
$a\,\overline x=\overline{\overline a\,x}$ for $a\in\mathbb C$, and
$$\langle\overline x,\overline y\rangle_{\overline H} :=\overline{\langle x,y\rangle_H}.$$
The canonical map $c_H:H\to\overline H$, $c_Hx=\overline x$, is a
conjugate-linear surjective isometry.

For complex Hilbert spaces $H_1,H_2$, a linear operator $A$ is a linear map
$A:D(A)\to H_2$ on a linear domain $D(A)\subseteq H_1$. Its graph is
$\Gamma(A)=\{(x,Ax):x\in D(A)\}\subseteq H_1\oplus H_2$, with the direct-sum
Hilbert norm. It is densely defined when $D(A)$ is dense in $H_1$, and closed
when $\Gamma(A)$ is closed.

For a densely defined linear operator $A:D(A)\subseteq H_1\to H_2$, define
$D(A^*)$ to consist of those $y\in H_2$ for which
$x\mapsto\langle Ax,y\rangle_{H_2}$ is bounded on $D(A)$ in the $H_1$ norm.
The bounded functional extends uniquely to $H_1$; its Riesz vector
$A^*y\in H_1$ is specified by
$$\langle Ax,y\rangle_{H_2}=\langle x,A^*y\rangle_{H_1} \qquad(x\in D(A)).$$
This defines the linear adjoint $A^*:D(A^*)\subseteq H_2\to H_1$.

An operator $S:D(S)\subseteq H\to H$ is **antilinear** when
$S(ax+by)=\overline a\,Sx+\overline b\,Sy$. Its associated linear operator
$\widetilde S:D(\widetilde S)\subseteq\overline H\to H$ is
$D(\widetilde S)=c_H(D(S))$ and
$\widetilde S(\overline x)=Sx$. For densely defined antilinear $S$, define
$$S^*:=c_H^{-1}\widetilde S^*,$$
on the domain $D(S^*)=D(\widetilde S^*)$. Thus $S^*$ is antilinear and
$$\langle Sx,y\rangle_H=\langle S^*y,x\rangle_H \qquad(x\in D(S),\ y\in D(S^*)).$$

items.title: Trace-class duality and finite-rank density
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let
$\mathcal S_1(H)$ be its trace-class operators with trace norm $\|\cdot\|_1$
and trace $\operatorname{Tr}$. Finite-rank operators are dense in
$(\mathcal S_1(H),\|\cdot\|_1)$. For every bounded linear functional
$\Phi:\mathcal S_1(H)\to\mathbb C$, there is a unique $X\in\mathcal B(H)$ such
that
$$\Phi(T)=\operatorname{Tr}(TX)\qquad(T\in\mathcal S_1(H)),$$
and the correspondence is isometric:
$\|\Phi\|=\|X\|$.

items.title: Polar decomposition of a closed densely defined operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H_1,H_2$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let
$A:D(A)\subseteq H_1\to H_2$ be a linear operator with dense domain and closed
graph. Define $A^*$ as in the local Hilbert-space adjoint convention. Then
$T:=A^*A$, on
$D(T)=\{x\in D(A):Ax\in D(A^*)\}$, is positive and self-adjoint. Its positive
square root $P:=T^{1/2}$ has domain $D(P)=D(A)$ and satisfies
$\|Px\|=\|Ax\|$ for every $x\in D(A)$. There is a unique partial isometry
$U:H_1\to H_2$ such that
$$A=UP,\qquad \ker U=\ker A.$$
Its initial space is $\overline{\operatorname{ran}P}=(\ker A)^\perp$ and its
final space is $\overline{\operatorname{ran}A}$. If $A$ is injective and has
dense range, then $U$ is unitary.

items.title: Strong closure and cyclic-separating duality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$R\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a unital star subalgebra. Its strong-operator
closure is $R''$. If $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ is a concrete von Neumann
algebra and $\Omega\in H$, then $\Omega$ is cyclic for $M$ exactly when it is
separating for $M'$.

items.title: Bounded increasing positive nets have strong suprema
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and
$M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ a concrete von Neumann algebra. Let $I$ be a
nonempty directed set, and let $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ be a net in $M$ such that each
$x_i$ is positive, $x_i\le x_j$ whenever $i\le j$, and
$\|x_i\|\le C$ for some finite $C\ge0$. Here $A\le B$ means that $A,B$ are
self-adjoint and $\langle A\xi,\xi\rangle\le\langle B\xi,\xi\rangle$ for every
$\xi\in H$. Then the net has a least upper bound $x=\sup_i x_i$ in $M_+$, and
$x_i\to x$ in the strong operator topology.

items.title: Closed antilinear polar calculus and Tomita-operator closability
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$S:D(S)\subseteq H\to H$ be a densely defined closable antilinear operator.
Its graph closure $\overline S$ is closed and has the polar decomposition
$$\overline S=J|\overline S|,\qquad |\overline S|=(\overline S^{\,*}\overline S)^{1/2}.$$
Here $J$ is antilinear, vanishes on $\ker\overline S$, and is isometric on
$(\ker\overline S)^\perp$; if $\overline S$ is injective and has dense range,
$J$ is antiunitary.

For a concrete von Neumann algebra $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ and a vector
$\Omega$ cyclic and separating for $M$, define
$D(S_0)=M\Omega$ and $S_0(x\Omega)=x^*\Omega$ for $x\in M$. Then $S_0$ is
well defined, densely defined, antilinear, and closable.

items.title: Trace-class quotient predual and normal functionals
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete von
Neumann algebra on a complex Hilbert space $H$, and define
$$M_\perp:=\{T\in\mathcal S_1(H):\operatorname{Tr}(Tx)=0 \text{ for every }x\in M\}.$$
Equip the coset space $Q:=\mathcal S_1(H)/M_\perp$ with the quotient norm.
Then the trace pairing
$$\Psi:M\to Q^*,\qquad (\Psi(x))([T])=\operatorname{Tr}(Tx),$$
is a well-defined isometric bijection, and $Q$ is a Banach space. Thus $Q$ is
an isometric predual of $M$, and its dual unit ball is weak-star compact.
Every vector functional $x\mapsto\langle x\xi,\xi\rangle$ and every positive
functional in $Q$ preserves suprema of bounded increasing positive nets in
$M$.

title: Von Neumann closure, standard vectors and modular analytic tools — Examples

items.title: Defining and Hilbert–Schmidt representations of M_n
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n>1$, let $H=\mathbb C^n$ with its standard
inner product linear in the first argument, and let $M=\mathcal B(H)=M_n(\mathbb
C)$ act on $H$ in its defining representation. Every nonzero vector in $H$ is
cyclic for $M$, but no vector in $H$ is separating for $M$.

Now let $\rho\in M$ be a faithful density matrix, meaning $\rho=\rho^*$,
$\langle\rho v,v\rangle>0$ for every nonzero $v\in H$, and
$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=1$. Let $K=M_n(\mathbb C)$ with the
Hilbert–Schmidt inner product
$$\langle X,Y\rangle_2:=\operatorname{Tr}(Y^*X),$$
and represent $M$ on $K$ by left multiplication $L_aX:=aX$. Then
$\{L_a:a\in M\}$ is a concrete von Neumann algebra on $K$, and
$\Omega:=\rho^{1/2}$ is a unit cyclic and separating vector for this
representation. Its vector functional is
$$\langle L_a\Omega,\Omega\rangle_2=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho a)\qquad(a\in M).$$
